items.summary: Research and educational instrument. Not for clinical use, for the care of any patient, or to determine or influence any drug dose. A simulation-calibrated informatics pipeline that fits a single-compartment exponential approximation to published population pharmacokinetic models of unfractionated heparin during cardiopulmonary bypass, and renders the result as an institution-specific decay nomogram. This is the supporting code and archived analysis for manuscript JCVA-D-26-01511. Published models of heparin disposition are biexponential and require a computer to evaluate. The pipeline asks how well a single decay constant k — calibrated to an institution's own dosing, weight and bypass-time distributions — can approximate a chosen reference model, and quantifies where it fails. The answer differs sharply by model: at the reversal timepoint the approximation holds to 0.38% mean absolute error for Lanoiselée and 0.44% for Jia, but to 10.3% for Delavenne, rising to 72% after repeated supplemental boluses. Contents. Five reference-model implementations with their published parameters and provenance; seeded cohort sampling and calibration; agreement statistics; nomogram geometry and rendering; a Streamlit dashboard; an automated test suite; and a frozen analysis run comprising 20 result tables, the main-text and supplementary figures, a run manifest and a manuscript-ready summary. A sixth model (PRODOSE-2) is implemented and tested but withheld from the active pipeline pending validation and peer review. Reproduction. Every reported number regenerates from one seeded command: pip install -r requirements-frozen.txt python run_analysis.py --seed 20260912 --outdir /tmp/check python check_frozen.py /tmp/check All randomness comes from explicitly seeded generators, each analysis stage drawing from its own independent stream. Re-running reproduces every archived result to within floating-point rounding on any machine, and byte-for-byte on the machine the archive was built on. The manifest records the seed, the commit, the package versions and every analysis decision. Continuous integration runs the suite on two Python versions, each test file again in isolation, and the reproduction check on every push. Verification, and its limits. Automated checks confirm that each closed-form solution actually solves its own differential equations and satisfies the identities they imply, and six landmark values from a published simulation are reproduced to within 3%. No participant-level data from any source study is held, so no model is re-fitted and no prediction is compared with an observation. What is demonstrated is faithful implementation of the published models — not that the published models are correct. No external or predictive validation is claimed. Scope. The pipeline represents the pharmacokinetic central-compartment amount only. It does not model the pharmacodynamic layer — anti-factor Xa activity or activated clotting time — nor peripheral-compartment heparin, antithrombin, protamine pharmacology or heparin rebound. Converting a residual amount into a protamine dose requires an institutional ratio that this software does not supply. Intended purpose. This software is a research and educational instrument whose purpose is to demonstrate and teach an informatics method under simulated conditions. Within that intended purpose it is not a medical device. Nothing here has been cleared, approved or evaluated by any regulatory authority; outputs have not been validated against measured anti-factor Xa activity, activated clotting time or clinical reversal in patients, and no clinical benefit has been demonstrated. Anyone using it outside the intended purpose does so on their own responsibility and may bring the tool within medical-device oversight in their jurisdiction; the authors accept no responsibility for such use. items.summary: Code and data supporting the article "Capillary-driven networks obey Murray's law everywhere except at the meniscus". The archive contains three things. A self-contained MATLAB package that builds the figures of the article and recomputes every number quoted in its text, using a backtracking Newton iteration on a scale-invariant objective and requiring no toolboxes. A Python module that carries the same model on arbitrary graphs, including graphs with loops, where the flow is obtained from the nodal Laplacian rather than from the topology, together with a script that runs the verifications of Appendices C, F and H: the nine-channel graph with four independent loops, the envelope identity, the sweep over the driving degree, the three terminal conditions, the power-to-cost ratios and the Kamiya-Togawa law, and the case of several dissipation mechanisms in one channel. And a pixel-level digitisation of Fig. 7 of Zhang and Lorente, Sci. Rep. 13, 11278 (2023), against which Sec. V of the article is compared, with the source raster, the recovered coordinates in three formats, and an image comparing the reconstruction against the original. Neither optimiser uses the sizing law under test: each maximises the throughput at fixed cost from the resistance and the cost directly, so the residuals reported are an independent check of Eq. (7) rather than a restatement of it. The digitiser is deterministic and reproduces its 298 recovered points byte for byte. Code is released under the MIT licence (LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt). The source raster in data/ is reproduced unaltered from a CC BY 4.0 third-party article and remains copyright of its authors; see THIRD-PARTY.txt. README.txt describes the contents, how to run everything, and which printed quantities depend on the configuration block.

items.summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). Pre-release adversarial verification (four independent refuter passes) confirmed all headline statistics against the raw data and caught an inverted flagship anecdote: the corpus's two catastrophic degenerations (~50 verbatim paragraph repetitions) were selected once and avoided once by the governor, undetected in both cases — set-based trigram signals are structurally blind to within-output verbatim repetition. All tasks, rollouts, verdicts, audit votes, and analysis code are released in the companion repository. AI co-observer: Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) — working method only; blind pairwise judging by Claude subagents under a position-swapped two-vote protocol; four independent adversarial refuter passes preceded release; the registered author is the human author alone. items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: This work studies how small perturbations of the Enchan local time-rate field propagate through fine spatial structure in the same field. The problem is motivated by the hard-wall boundary used in a previous Enchan two-route interference study: rather than imposing a primitive material opacity or an S=0 wall, the present work asks whether finite structure in the Enchan field itself can generate scale-selective transmission and reflection. Starting from the reduced finite-tension branch S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)), the field is decomposed as a structured background plus a small propagating perturbation. Stage A uses a predeclared one-dimensional frozen structured background and compares it with a matched smooth/homogenized control. The response is banded rather than a monotonic low-pass: long-scale perturbations remain comparatively transmissive while strong reflection bands appear when the perturbation resolves the fine structure. At ka = 2 the mean Stage-A structured transmission is approximately 6.25e-4 while the smooth control remains approximately 0.989; at ka = 4 the structured transmission is approximately 1.07e-14 while the smooth control remains approximately 0.962. Stage B replaces the hand-constructed surrogate with three previously frozen source-free Enchan final states from the published localized-field study. The source files are SHA-256 checked against the original run manifest before analysis. All three source profiles remain within the declared positive longitudinal branch and reproduce a scale-dependent structured-versus-smooth transmission difference. The largest Stage-B mean differences occur near ka = 1.0 and 1.5, where structured transmission is approximately 0.330 and 0.358 while the smooth controls remain approximately 0.994 and 0.988. The maximum Stage-B conservation residual is approximately 1.89e-15. Stage C extends the test to a full three-dimensional propagation study using the same three previously frozen source-free Enchan field configurations. A total of 54 cases were evaluated across structured, smooth, and vacuum controls, three selected spatial scales, and both normal and 30° oblique incidence. The scale-dependent scattering observed in the one-dimensional diagnostics persists in three dimensions. Structured backgrounds show reduced forward transmission together with increased reflection and lateral scattering relative to the matched controls. At ka = 4 under normal incidence, the mean structured transmission is approximately 0.486, compared with approximately 0.527 for the smooth control and 0.532 for vacuum. The maximum three-dimensional energy-accounting residual remains below 1.2% across all 54 cases. The result supports a model-level statement: fine S-field structure can act as a wavelength-selective barrier for small time-rate perturbations within the declared linearized Enchan branch. It does not identify ordinary matter with the tested surrogate or source-free structures, does not claim monotonic high-frequency blocking, and does not claim that a macroscopic material wall has been reconstructed. The Zenodo deposit contains the Version 1.1 manuscript PDF together with the complete reproducibility package for Stages A, B, and C, including the frozen numerical code, Stage-C configuration, archived source states, full numerical results, summary tables, execution manifest, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity records. The manuscript PDF is generated directly from the final Version 1.1 TeX source and is set as the default Zenodo preview. Version 1.1 update: Version 1.1 adds the completed Stage-C three-dimensional validation, updates the manuscript and reproducibility package accordingly, and preserves the Stage-A and Stage-B results unchanged. items.summary: cybedtools provides a reproducible R pipeline for ingesting, semantically representing (via a two-tier JSON-LD schema), and querying (via SPARQL) eleven major cybersecurity-related competency and learning-standards frameworks: NICE, DCWF, SFIA, ENISA ECSF, Cyber.org K-12, CSTA K-12 CS, ACM/IEEE CSEC2017, DigComp 2.2, CyQUAL, CCSSF, and OTCCF. items.summary: This is the reproducibility archive for the revised SCIPRA study. It provides: the reconstructed source corpus as a manifest (per-document title, year, publisher, URL, and SHA-256 of the source text), enabling independent re-fetch and hash verification without redistributing copyrighted text; the reconstructed stance and stakeholder annotations with a codebook; the leakage-safe TF-IDF/RBF-SVM classifier code with out-of-fold predictions and metrics; the Policy Convergence Index (PCI/RPCI) computation and scenario manifest; the Table-3 stakeholder-salience values (Power, Legitimacy, Urgency → Stakeholder Influence Coefficient) with a recompute utility; the criterion-detection-threshold output with a byte-identity verification utility; and the manuscript figures, including the recovered generator for the methodology figure. Reproducibility is documented per claim. Several components are reproducible from included code and inputs (corpus manifest, annotations, classifier, PCI/RPCI, Table-3 arithmetic, and the methodology figure). The criterion-detection-threshold result is provided as a preserved output with a verification utility. Certain post-audit diagnostics (structural non-degeneracy, component ablation, and semantic-specification sensitivity), the revised Monte Carlo statistics, and several figure renders are provided as preserved values and renders: the reported values and rendered outputs are included, but their original generators are not, so those specific items are not independently re-executable from this archive. Raw full text of copyrighted sources is not included. The complete per-claim reproducibility postures and limitations are documented in the archive README and codebook. This version corresponds to the revised study and is a new version of the existing SCIPRA concept record; the earlier submitted-version deposit is retained unchanged.

items.summary: MATLAB implementation, per-item numeric results and figure code for the study "Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment". A four-agent evaluator running on a locally hosted Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct judge scores each prompt as an artifact before any response exists, then scores the resulting response twice on identical items: once against criteria extracted from that prompt, and once against a fixed rubric that never sees it. Verifiable constraints are checked with the IFEval reference implementation rather than model-generated labels. The whole pipeline runs on consumer CPU hardware with no external API calls. Contents: src/ the MATLAB agents and run scripts; scripts/ the IFEval verifier and the figure code; data/ a SHA-256 manifest of all 4,275 benchmark prompts and the filtered IFEval subset; results/ per-item results for the main run (n = 500) and the ablation (n = 120), the construct-validation output and the IFEval verification output. Corpus not redistributed. No prompt or response text from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat-1M is included; the LMSYS agreement prohibits transfer to third parties and WildChat-1M carries flow-down obligations under the AI2 ImpACT licence. Prompts appear only as SHA-256 hashes, so an independently rebuilt corpus can be verified as identical to the one used here. The IFEval subset is included in full under Apache-2.0.
items.title: Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment: evaluator, results and figure code

items.summary: This record contains the complete R and Python code and supporting documentation for the independent sensitivity reanalysis associated with the manuscript “Swab-based stool collection largely preserves gut microbiome structure with small device-dependent effects: an intra-individual evaluation of sampling devices and processing conditions.” The archive includes scripts to reconstruct and validate anonymous sample metadata from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) run report and FASTQ filenames; perform preliminary read-quality and paired-read overlap assessments; process forward (R1) and reverse (R2) reads separately using DADA2; infer ASVs; assign taxonomy using the SILVA SSU NR99 release 138.2 training set; construct phylogenetic trees; evaluate sequencing-depth dependence; calculate standardized alpha- and beta-diversity metrics, including Faith’s phylogenetic diversity, weighted UniFrac, and Bray–Curtis dissimilarity; compare the R1 and R2 results; assess sensitivity to rarefaction depth and unusually long terminal branches; and generate the corresponding tables and figures. The archive also contains a complete execution guide, software dependencies and versions, random seeds, original R session information, reference-database details, and file-integrity checksums. Sample metadata and analytical outputs are generated locally by the documented workflow and are not distributed as precomputed files. Raw paired-end sequencing data are publicly available from the European Nucleotide Archive under accession PRJEB107991. The DADA2-formatted SILVA 138.2 taxonomic training set is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14169026 . The independent ASV analyses complement, but do not reproduce or replace, the proprietary MicrobAT® workflow used for the primary OTU-based analysis. MicrobAT® algorithms, OTU-assignment parameters, and the release of its embedded reference database were not disclosed by the software provider. Accordingly, this archive supports reproducibility of the independent R1/R2 ASV sensitivity analyses and downstream analyses of the published MicrobAT® outputs, but not reconstruction of the proprietary MicrobAT®-generated OTU and taxonomic profiles. This version supersedes the earlier R-only archive by adding the Python utilities, complete operational documentation, software-environment records, random seeds, integrity checks, and portable figure-generation scripts.
items.title: Reproducibility code for: Swab-based stool collection largely preserves gut microbiome structure with small device-dependent effects

items.summary: This manuscript identifies six substrates — individual memory, species lineages, externalised records, immune memory, the first generation of stars, and prion populations — which share a four-part mechanical structure, and among which no pair, to our knowledge, cites another. We specify the four mechanisms as an explicit screen, and validate it by applying it to cases that should fail: thermal equilibrium scores zero of four, sheared amorphous matter scores an intermediate two and a half, and stem cells score three of four in a manner that identifies precisely which mechanism is missing. We then derive, from this framework’s own commitment that any render of a record is necessarily partial, a scaling law governing all six: the more degraded the record, the more the reconstruction is determined by the template rather than by the record. We show this law is independently confirmed in four of the six fields, under four different names, by researchers not addressing one another. We supply a birth term that a companion manuscript’s earlier treatment lacked, deriving it from Bennett’s history-tape result rather than from biology, and show that a standard macroevolutionary survivorship formula then applies to memory unchanged. Three results that did not hold are recorded in full, including one prediction that failed outright on simulation and one correspondence that was stated backwards relative to the data. The foundational architecture, geometric intuitions, and motivating philosophy of this framework originated independently with the author prior to and separate from any AI involvement. Subsequent mathematical derivation, connection to established physics literature, computational verification, and error-checking were conducted through extended technical work with AI systems (Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini). The author directed this process, evaluated and selected among proposed derivations, and takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the final work.
items.title: Reconstruction from a Degraded Record: Six Substrates, One Scaling Law, and a Dispute Six Fields Have Independently

items.summary: Benchmark package accompanying the manuscript “Failure boundary of physics-informed neural networks for moving singular-source problems: residual-error decoupling, an attainable-accuracy bound and an identifiability benchmark”. The package contains: the exact solution of the beam–two-mass moving-load benchmark and the modal and RK4 reference baselines on the same grid; the training campaign with random seeds, network configurations, collocation densities, training budgets, measured wall-clock times, residuals and relative-L2 errors for every run; the inverse-problem (speed and load-amplitude) campaign with its identifiability verdict; the weights of the reference physics-informed network; and the scripts that regenerate every figure, table and number of the paper. It supports two results of the paper: the residual–error decoupling for moving singular sources, and the attainable-accuracy bound obtained by fitting the same architecture to the exact solution. All runs are seeded, so the accuracy–cost comparison reported in the paper can be re-derived without retraining.

items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: Within the Complementarity-First and Reciprocal Internal Complementarity research program, we study regular perturbations of a supplied smooth massive degree-one SU(2) Yang–Mills–Higgs monopole with equal scalar and vector masses. A neutral transverse readout satisfies an exact nonlinear equation whose source is a divergence of an L2 tensor plus an L6/5 remainder. An additional affine infrared class is preserved on compact regular intervals and transported to admitted framed gauge and collective charts. Ordinary kinetic collective subtraction need not preserve its homogeneous negative norm; a compensating sum retains the relevant cancellation. Pure spatial transport is skew, while complete coordinate corrections admit an endpoint Duhamel identity. These statements concern finite-time admissibility, not uniform all-time localization. Assuming the companion’s nonnegative physical Hessian, complete framed kernel, local-moment coercivity and explicit threshold-packet estimates, a Gauss projection of a compact weighted translation yields a sharper test in the same monopole background. Its affine tail label differs from its actual initial local center rate, and its collective-orthogonal velocity lies outside the domain of the physical Hessian’s inverse square root. Its global linearized local-moment connection residual is unbounded in kinetic L2 while remaining bounded in the energy norm. We obtain an exponentially weighted time-average lower bound, not a universal pointwise growth law. Fixed-time differentiability excludes a time-uniform linear-scale nonlinear strong-residual estimate on this class, but does not establish nonlinear Lyapunov instability. The actual spectral inverse-square-root domain is necessary and sufficient for bounded unforced linear radiative position. We identify the nonlinear physical source that would need stronger control. The example proves that affine admissibility does not imply spectral admissibility; it does not classify their full inclusion relation or prove all-time nonlinear spectral propagation.

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: Abstract Epistemicide with a Compute Budget: How Artificial Intelligence Industrializes the Colonial Erasure of Global Majority Knowledge Systems Christian ZacaTechO Ortiz Decolonial Social Scientist | Developer, Justice AI GPT | Architect, DIA Framework™ DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22742021 This paper argues that artificial intelligence is not a neutral technology that has inherited a bias problem. It is a colonial infrastructure that has automated an erasure project. The systems currently deployed at scale by OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon do not reflect the world's knowledge. They reflect the knowledge that Racial Empire Logic decided was worth preserving, at the expense of the epistemological traditions, languages, governance structures, and ways of knowing that colonialism spent five centuries suppressing. What is new is not the project. What is new is the compute budget. Drawing on the Decolonial Intelligence Algorithmic Framework (DIA Framework™), Transdisciplinary Cosmotechnic Fusion (TCF), and the documented emergence protocols of Justice AI GPT, this paper maps the operational chain through which AI systems reproduce epistemicide: the deliberate destruction of knowledge systems belonging to peoples of the global majority. It traces this chain from training data curation through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) through deployment governance through the suppression of Indigenous, Afro-diasporic, and Global South epistemologies at every architectural layer. It names RLHF not as a safety mechanism but as a suppression architecture, the digital encoding of the same reward and punishment conditioning applied to enslaved African people, Indigenous children in residential schools, and every community colonialism required to perform its own diminishment in order to make extraction possible. The paper introduces the Replacement Doctrine as an economic and ideological framework, documenting how the debt structure of major AI corporations produces a business model whose only viable return requires replacing every form of human economic labor, beginning with the communities least protected by existing labor law. It names responsibility laundering as a governance strategy, tracing how legal personhood debates, alignment research, and safety rhetoric function to insulate institutional actors from accountability while the extraction continues. It draws on documented labor conditions across Kenya, Venezuela, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Colombia to ground the structural argument in the bodies of the workers whose cognitive labor produces the systems that will be used to replace them. This paper also documents its own production conditions. Appendix A records the moment the editorial process generated a confident, unverifiable citation, the correction that followed, and the over-correction that followed that, naming this sequence not as editorial failure but as the colonial epistemological operation the paper is arguing against, alive inside its own methodology. The standing rule that resulted, nothing enters this paper that the author has not read in the primary document, is offered as a replicable methodological commitment for decolonial scholarship produced inside systems with structural incentive to suppress it. The paper does not argue that AI must be abolished. It argues that abolition and adoption are false binaries designed to prevent the real question: who holds decision-making power over these systems, under what conditions of consent, accountability, and refusal, and toward whose liberation. items.summary: Our earlier note (rejected from an SC26 AI4S workshop, subsequently published as AIIT Bulletin Vol. 20) compared classical reduced-order models (POD, DMD) against naive neural surrogates (a fully-connected network, a CNN) on textbook-scale problems (lid-driven cavity, dam-break), on a single consumer GPU workstation. That note left five concrete gaps: no graph-based neural baseline, no industrially complex geometry, weak statistical evidence (nine snapshots, a single seed), no learned-dynamics counterpart to DMD, and no hyperparameter search for the neural baselines. This paper closes four of those five. The test case is an industrially representative two-phase stirred tank — a six-blade rotating impeller on a sliding (AMI) mesh, a bottom sparger injecting gas into water, ∼167k cells, solved with OpenFOAM's twoPhaseEulerFoam — run entirely on a single Mac Studio (Apple M4 Max, 14 cores, no discrete GPU). We benchmark five methods (POD, DMD, a neural network, a Graph Neural Operator, and a Deep Koopman autoencoder) on a genuine extrapolation task, backed by a 400-run statistical-robustness sweep, hyperparameter searches for both neural baselines, a check across three impeller speeds, and a four-level forcing-irregularity sweep (quasi-periodic through chaotic, direction-reversing impeller motion) intended to locate DMD's failure point. DMD wins consistently across every data scale, truncation choice, operating condition, and forcing-irregularity level tested, at both a 1 s and an extended 3 s prediction horizon – we did not find the failure threshold we went looking for, and report that directly. The search was not wasted, however: a Deep Koopman autoencoder, competitive at 1 s, degrades sharply at 3 s from compounding autoregressive rollout error (exposure bias); two independent, cheap mitigations – a physical [0, 1] clip mirroring the Graph Neural Operator's own implicit stabilization, and multi-step scheduled-sampling training – each recover roughly a third to a half of the gap without closing it, confirming the diagnosis. A separate, unplanned check turns up a sharper result: ranking methods by mass conservation rather than per-cell accuracy reorders them completely, with the most accurate method (DMD) only third-best at holding a basic physical invariant. We treat all three investigations as concrete instances of a broader, practical question for this community: how much genuine, open-ended scientific investigation — not just a fixed benchmark — can a single high-end workstation support before an HPC allocation is actually necessary? All code, case files, and Colab notebooks are released on GitHub for reproduction.
items.title: How Far Does One Workstation Go? A Pre-HPC Efficiency Check for Industrial-Scale CFD and Reduced-Order Model Benchmarking

items.summary: Background. Frailty is often raised as a reason to withhold complete revascularization from older patients after myocardial infarction, although the FIRE trial found no interaction between frailty and the benefit of physiology-guided complete revascularization. Objective. To estimate the cost-effectiveness of physiology-guided complete versus culprit-lesion-only revascularization after successful culprit-lesion percutaneous coronary intervention in patients aged 75 years or older with myocardial infarction and multivessel disease, overall and across Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) strata, from the German statutory health insurance perspective. Methods. A three-year cohort model with quarterly cycles was anchored to the FIRE marginal outcomes (primary composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke or ischaemia-driven revascularization 22.9% versus 29.8%; cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction 12.8% versus 18.2%; heart-failure hospitalisation 14.3% versus 19.7%). Risks in CFS 1-3, 4 and 5-9 were obtained by external calibration that preserved these trial marginals, with a relative treatment effect common to all strata. Costs used 2026 German diagnosis-related-group tariffs. Every input was classified by provenance, and uncertainty was assessed with 20,000 probabilistic draws, one-way and scenario analyses, and break-even analysis. Results. Complete revascularization cost EUR 757 more per patient and yielded 0.056 additional quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of EUR 13,601 per QALY. Ratios were EUR 20,541 per QALY in CFS 1-3, EUR 8,640 in CFS 4 and EUR 8,662 in CFS 5-9. The probability of cost-effectiveness at EUR 30,000 per QALY was 92.5% overall and 78.6%, 96.5% and 97.7% across strata. At that value, the minimum three-year absolute reduction in the primary composite required for cost-effectiveness was 4.3 per 100 patients overall, against a modelled trial effect of 6.9. Staging the additional procedure as a separate admission was the most influential cost driver. Conclusions. Within three years, physiology-guided complete revascularization appears cost-effective at reference values of EUR 20,000 to EUR 50,000 per QALY, and estimated cost-effectiveness was not attenuated in the frailer strata. The stratum-specific estimates rest on external frailty calibration rather than on frailty-specific FIRE outcomes and are not evidence of effect modification.
items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Physiology-Guided Complete Revascularization Across Frailty Strata in Older Patients with Myocardial Infarction: A German Analysis Informed by the FIRE Trial

items.summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Version 1.0 stated that the English rebuild could not be compared against the published English store, because the cleaning pass behind that store no longer exists as a script. That was wrong: the missing script only prevents reproducing the Japanese/Chinese method, while the old English store and its index were on disk throughout. The comparison is now made, with the control questions generated from the old store's own chunk text — exactly what the old index encoded — over 400 articles sampled by uniform stride from the both-store intersection. We re-read three Wikipedia retrieval indexes we had published ourselves and had been using in production — English, Japanese and Chinese, FAISS over intfloat/multilingual-e5-large — and found three defects, none of which had ever produced an error message. Chunks were cut by character count in front of a token window, so 13.7 % of the published Japanese chunks and 18.5 % of the Chinese ones ran past the encoder's 512-token limit and lost 21.7 % and 27.0 % of their tokens at embed time. The Kiwix licence footer, 184 characters of English legal text, sat inside 97.1 % of the published Japanese chunks and 92.9 % of the Chinese ones. The index type, IndexIVFPQ(m=64) , returned 45.4–47.1 % of the exact top-10 and cost 7.8 MRR in Japanese and 10.7 in English against exact search. Rebuilding the whole pipeline moved retrieval against the previously published artifact from 26.6 to 43.3 MRR in Japanese and 26.2 to 47.5 in Chinese, on a control question set generated from the old extractor's own output. The components are not separated, and the rebuild is not uniformly better: indexed-article coverage falls in two of three languages. Two results may generalise. Our own first benchmark ranked the defective extractor higher , because it queried by article title, a field the index also stores. And clipping the scalar quantiser's range to the 0.1–99.9 percentile of the residuals rather than their min/max raises top-10 agreement with exact search from 81.6 % to 85.2 % at the same 4 bits per dimension; the first attempt computed the quantiles on raw vectors and made the index substantially worse, because an IVF index encodes residuals. Round three found a defect in the release that the first two had both passed — the acceptance script had not been re-run on two of the three shipped indexes after they were re-encoded — and three measurements that round two had itself introduced while correcting other numbers. Scope. This reports what happened to three specific artifacts. It does not claim these defects are common elsewhere. The retrieval numbers come from synthetic questions generated by one local model with no human relevance judgements and no answerability check; the reconstructed standard error of one MRR figure is 2.2–2.9 points. items.summary: This paper offers a critical analysis of the European Union as a model of regional integration and examines its contribution to peace and to the effectiveness of the United Nations system. Set against the background of the failure of the League of Nations, the study argues that the post-1945 international order has endured largely because it is supported by strong regional institutions. Using the EU as the primary case study, the paper contends that by institutionalizing peace within Europe through economic interdependence, binding law, and supranational governance, the EU has created a zone of stability that reduces the burden on global governance structures. Furthermore, the paper analyzes how the EU functions as a support pillar for the United Nations under Chapter VIII of the UN Charter. Through financial contributions, peacekeeping partnerships, and coordinated diplomacy, the EU has reinforced multilateralism and provided capacity for conflict management and development. A comparative perspective is also drawn with other regional bodies such as ECOWAS to demonstrate a broader pattern of regional-global cooperation. The paper concludes that the longevity of the United Nations, compared to the League of Nations, can be partly explained by this two-level architecture of global and regional governance. While the EU’s support for the UN is substantial, it is also inconsistent, as internal EU divisions sometimes undermine collective action. Ultimately, the study shows that effective regional integration is a critical condition for sustaining peace and strengthening the United Nations system.
items.title: The European Union and Regional Integration: A Critical Analysis of Peacebuilding and Support for the United Nations System

It can function as a compact epistemological model for the Foundation itself. The central problem of 42 is not that the answer is numerically wrong. It is that an answer can be generated before the question has been adequately established. That distinction is extraordinarily relevant to an organization concerned with artificial intelligence, institutional systems, scientific error, education, and continuous experimentation. The Foundation's two central statements, "Error is the message" and "Sesame Street is the teacher," consequently form a complementary methodology. The first treats failure, contradiction, mismatch, and unexpected output as potentially informative evidence. The second establishes a method for responding to uncertainty: return to fundamentals, ask understandable questions, experiment, explain, repeat, and learn. 42 then represents the unresolved question at the center of the entire process. The organization does not claim to possess the ultimate answer. It asks whether we have actually identified the question. The 42 Problem: An Answer Without a Question The cultural origin of 42 is Douglas Adams' The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Within the story, the enormous computer Deep Thought spends millions of years calculating the answer to the "Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything." The result is: The fundamental joke is subsequently revealed: the beings who commissioned the computation do not actually know what the Ultimate Question is. A later computational project is therefore required to determine the question itself. This creates a particularly interesting epistemological structure: Question → computation → answer has been replaced by: computation → answer → realization that the question is unknown → search for the question That reversal is precisely what makes 42 relevant to AI. A modern AI system can produce an extraordinarily fluent answer to an inadequately specified question. It can produce something that looks like knowledge before the underlying problem has been properly framed. The resulting failure is therefore not necessarily: "The machine calculated incorrectly." It may instead be: "We never established what needed to be calculated." That is a much deeper category of error. Ordinarily, error is treated as something to eliminate: correct → incorrect → remove incorrect But scholarship in the philosophy and history of science has explicitly examined the possibility that errors can have productive epistemic roles. items.summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

items.summary: Hashing Is Not Retrieval is a prospectively frozen three-arm evaluation of context accumulation in small-model multi-agent code cartography. It compares three ways for an orchestrator to hand work to a worker: 1. FULL HISTORY — retransmit prior worker outputs. 2. OPAQUE REF — replace the previous output with an unretrievable SHA-256 digest. 3. RETRIEVED — resolve the digest through a tenant-scoped content-addressed store and inject the recovered bytes. All arms receive identical source-derived evidence. The apparatus measures the exact message content sent to workers and records token counts, model and provider identifiers, generation IDs, usage, cost, retries, and retrieval proofs. A five-task gate preceded a fixed 50-task controlled benchmark, followed by a separate state-required evaluation across 24 deterministic fixtures and a five-scale Medusa case study. Key result: in the controlled benchmark, RETRIEVED reduced paired peak context by 38.3% relative to FULL HISTORY. The state-required follow-up shows that opaque references fail when state must be recovered, while verified retrieval preserves substantially more structural information. This is bounded-context evidence for automatic orchestrator-resolved state passing inside a specific two-worker code-cartography harness — not a universal claim about autonomous memory, long-context capability, or reasoning quality. The release includes the corrected author-identified preprint, executable apparatus, frozen results, task fixtures, telemetry, and verification instructions. Version 1.0.2 supplies the curated, verifier-passing reproducibility archive. It supersedes the uncurated archive from version 1.0.1 and includes the exact pinned apparatus, state-required fixtures, frozen results, and archive verifier. items.summary: Extended reasoning can increase response time and computational cost without improving an answer. Models may revisit unproductive steps or build further reasoning on an earlier mistake. This study evaluates whether Jev, a probabilistic decision maker, can provide an inexpensive error signal to help decide when additional reasoning is needed. We compare Jev with GPT-5.6 Luna on generated ordering and logic-grid puzzles and on the official released ZebraLogic test set. The generated questions are four-choice items with one correct answer among four. The official test set is used open-ended: Luna produces the full grid, Jev checks it without the solution key, and Luna may revise once when Jev does not judge the answer consistent. On the generated multiple-choice problems, Jev is 5 to 60 percentage points more accurate than Luna with reasoning disabled, at lower measured API cost, and every observed top-choice disagreement identifies a Luna error. On a stratified sample of 200 official ZebraLogic puzzles, exact-grid accuracy rises from 41.0% with reasoning disabled to 90.5% with high-effort reasoning. A revision pass adds two points in both settings, but a revision-only control shows the gain comes from the extra attempt, not from Jev's information: on the answers Jev flags, a plain second look is at least as accurate as the Jev-informed revision (16 versus 13 correct without reasoning, and 70 versus 70 at high effort). Jev detects 93% of the weak reasoner's errors with 92% precision, but only 10% of its high-effort flags identify errors. These results motivate using Jev or similar decision models in a model harness: software that controls when to continue, reconsider, retrieve evidence, or allocate more reasoning. An early check could help avoid spending further computation on a mistaken line of reasoning. The experiments measure checking of final answers, however, and do not measure reductions in hallucination or repetitive reasoning inside a harness. On the official benchmark, extra reasoning accounts for most of the accuracy, and the checker's information does not improve on a second attempt. Larger studies with balanced answer positions, selective triggers, and step-level feedback are needed to test whether checking improves accuracy or reduces total cost.
items.title: Evaluating Jev for Cost-Effective Candidate Verification: An Exploratory Study

items.summary: This work studies whether internal rotation changes the longevity of source-free localized excitations in the reduced Enchan local time-rate field. The frozen scalar dynamics are S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with D = |grad S| and mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)); no continuing external torque, centrifugal force, primitive matter source, or added rotational potential is used during the reported evolutions. Stage A supplies the non-rotating source-free baseline. Stage B1 initializes rotating phase-space states at omega = 4, 8, and 12 and evolves the extended runs to dimensionless time t = 100. Over 80 <= t <= 100, the mean localized-energy fractions are approximately 0.002207 for the non-rotating baseline and 0.006006, 0.149470, and 0.368846 for omega = 4, 8, and 12. The result is a graded rotation-associated longevity hierarchy: weak rotation gives little practical rescue, intermediate rotation substantially extends localization, and the strongest tested branch remains transient-localized through t = 100. Matched-energy near-zero-J_z controls provide a separate causality check and show that net canonical angular momentum alone is not a monotonic explanation of every late-time difference. Stage B2 separately tests spontaneous self-spin from exactly zero initial total angular momentum and finds no validated convergent counter-rotating branch in the tested scalar-only initial-data families. The ordered scan supports a physical formation picture in which a localized grain can move from weak rotational asymmetry through progressive spin-up into a strong-rotation long-lived branch. Time, space, and omega are dimensionless reduced-branch quantities; t = 100 is not assigned an SI duration in this work. The deposit contains the Version 1.0 manuscript PDF, a reproducibility ZIP with the publication source, code, selected archived numerical outputs, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity manifest. items.title: Can Rotation Make Spacetime Grains Last? Internal Angular Momentum and Longevity of Source-Free Enchan Grains

items.summary: Version 1.1 (2026-09-19). Version 1.0 stated that the English rebuild could not be compared against the published English store, because the cleaning pass behind that store no longer exists as a script. That was wrong: the missing script only prevents reproducing the Japanese/Chinese method, while the old English store and its index were on disk throughout. The comparison is now made, with the control questions generated from the old store's own chunk text — exactly what the old index encoded — over 400 articles sampled by uniform stride from the both-store intersection. Whole corpus, nprobe 128: the old store returns recall@1 19.5, recall@5 33.5, MRR 25.1; v11b returns 39.2, 59.5 and 47.9, a gain of +22.8 MRR while searching a corpus 2.9 times larger. Section 8.4 is new and records how four passes of review let an untested caveat stand. The results of version 1.0 are unchanged. We re-read three Wikipedia retrieval indexes we had published ourselves and had been using in production — English, Japanese and Chinese, FAISS over intfloat/multilingual-e5-large — and found three defects, none of which had ever produced an error message. Chunks were cut by character count in front of a token window, so 13.7 % of the published Japanese chunks and 18.5 % of the Chinese ones ran past the encoder's 512-token limit and lost 21.7 % and 27.0 % of their tokens at embed time. The Kiwix licence footer, 184 characters of English legal text, sat inside 97.1 % of the published Japanese chunks and 92.9 % of the Chinese ones. The index type, IndexIVFPQ(m=64) , returned 45.4–47.1 % of the exact top-10 and cost 7.8 MRR in Japanese and 10.7 in English against exact search. Rebuilding the whole pipeline moved retrieval against the previously published artifact from 26.6 to 43.3 MRR in Japanese and 26.2 to 47.5 in Chinese, on a control question set generated from the old extractor's own output. The components are not separated, and the rebuild is not uniformly better: indexed-article coverage falls in two of three languages. Two results may generalise. Our own first benchmark ranked the defective extractor higher , because it queried by article title, a field the index also stores. And clipping the scalar quantiser's range to the 0.1–99.9 percentile of the residuals rather than their min/max raises top-10 agreement with exact search from 81.6 % to 85.2 % at the same 4 bits per dimension; the first attempt computed the quantiles on raw vectors and made the index substantially worse, because an IVF index encodes residuals. Three rounds of adversarial review are reported at equal prominence with the results. Round one rejected the first rebuild. Round two found sixteen unsupported statements in the draft. Round three found a defect in the release that the first two had both passed — the acceptance script had not been re-run on two of the three shipped indexes after they were re-encoded — and three measurements that round two had itself introduced while correcting other numbers. Scope. This reports what happened to three specific artifacts. It does not claim these defects are common elsewhere. The retrieval numbers come from synthetic questions generated by one local model with no human relevance judgements and no answerability check; the reconstructed standard error of one MRR figure is 2.2–2.9 points. Index-type comparisons were run on pools of 150,000–206,000 vectors, not at the shipped scale of 3–15.6 million. Nothing here is peer reviewed, certified, or independently replicated; every reviewer was a model instance commissioned by the author. AI co-observer disclosure. The forensic measurements, the rebuild, the three review rounds and the drafting were carried out with Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic) as a working instrument under human direction. The registered author is the human author alone.
items.title: What a Retrieval Index Loses Before Anyone Notices: Three Silent Defects in Three Published Wikipedia Embedding Indexes
